page.layout: One column of running text; a sermon heading ("CONCIO V.") with its scripture reference above the text; a decorated woodcut initial at the start of the sermon. Running head at the top with the page number at the right. No margins, no notes, no catchword.

main_text.p: audiet, quia facies meretricis facta est tibi, sine pudore effecta es ad omnes. Veluti meretrix ergo punietur, & filij eius ad occisionem præparari videbuntur. Dominus Deus noster liberet atque seruet nos ab omni immundo & meretricio spiritu per Christum Iesum, Amen.
main_text.head: CONCIO V. Genes. 12.

p.i: ERat autem fames in illa terra, & ob id descendit Abram in Aegyptum, ut peregrinaretur ibi: nam erat grauis fames in terra. Et factum est cum applicasset ut intraret in Aegyptum, dixit ad Sarai uxorem suam: En scio quod tu sis mulier pulchro aspectu. Erit itaque, quando viderint te Aegyptij, dicet: uxor illius est hæc, & interficient me, te vero in vita conseruabunt. Dic obsecro quod soror mea sis, ut scilicet bene sit mihi propter te, et viuat anima mea tui causa. Factum itaq; est, cum venisset Abram in Aegyptum, contemplati sunt Aegyptij mulierem: nam erat valde pulchra. Viderunt quoq; eam principes Pharaonis,

page.notes: The woodcut initial is a decorated capital, read here as E (joined to "Rat" as "ERat"); the letter is not fully clear, so it is a probable reading. The word "peregrinare / tur" is broken at the line end without a printed hyphen and is written whole. The first line of the sermon's continuation has a dot-like mark in "f.cies", read as "facies". Abbreviations itaq; and quoq; are kept as printed. The heading "Genef. 12." is printed with the long-s form and is copied as "Genes. 12." with the s normalised.
